# I. Data Importation & Initial Exploration

*Loading and understanding the structure of soil and yield datasets*

## I.1. Dataset Loading and Basic Information

*Import the soil database with proper encoding and delimiter settings, then display fundamental dataset characteristics including dimensions and column structure*

```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/U078-N800/Desktop/Ml_Internship/Copy")
# Load the data - using semicolon as separator based on the CSV structure
soil_data <- read.csv("BD_soil.csv", sep = ";", dec = ",", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "latin1")


# Display basic information about the dataset
cat("Dataset dimensions:", dim(data), "\n")
cat("Number of rows:", nrow(data), "\n")
cat("Number of columns:", ncol(data), "\n")

# Display column names
cat("\nColumn names:\n")
print(colnames(data))
str(soil_data)
print(colnames(soil_data))

# Unique and sorted
unique_parc_detaillee <- sort(unique(soil_data$Parc.Detaillee))
unique_parcelle <- sort(unique(data$Parcelle))

# Display with numbering
cat("📌 Unique Parc.Detaillee values:\n")
for (i in seq_along(unique_parc_detaillee)) {
  cat(paste0(i, ". ", unique_parc_detaillee[i], "\n"))
}

cat("\n📌 Unique Parcelle values:\n")
for (i in seq_along(unique_parcelle)) {
  cat(paste0(i, ". ", unique_parcelle[i], "\n"))
}

```

## I.2. Data Standardization & Quality Assessment

### I.2.1. Parcel Name Standardization

*Convert parcel identifiers to uppercase to ensure consistency across datasets for accurate matching*

```{r}
# Step 1: Convert to uppercase
soil_data$Parc.Detaillee <- toupper(soil_data$Parc.Detaillee)
data$Parcelle <- toupper(data$Parcelle)

# Step 2: Get unique sorted values
unique_parc_detaillee <- sort(unique(soil_data$Parc.Detaillee))
unique_parcelle <- sort(unique(data$Parcelle))

# Step 3: Display with count and numbered list

cat("📌 Unique values in soil_data$Parc.Detaillee:\n")
cat(paste0("Total: ", length(unique_parc_detaillee), " unique entries\n\n"))
for (i in seq_along(unique_parc_detaillee)) {
  cat(paste0(i, ". ", unique_parc_detaillee[i], "\n"))
}

cat("\n📌 Unique values in data$Parcelle:\n")
cat(paste0("Total: ", length(unique_parcelle), " unique entries\n\n"))
for (i in seq_along(unique_parcelle)) {
  cat(paste0(i, ". ", unique_parcelle[i], "\n"))
}

```

### 2. Frequency Analysis of Parcels

*Analyze the distribution of samples across different parcels to identify data density*

```{r}
# Step 2: Count frequencies

data_freq <- sort(table(data$Parcelle), decreasing = TRUE)

for (i in seq_along(data_freq)) {
  cat(paste0(i, ". ", names(data_freq)[i], " – ", data_freq[i], " sample(s)\n"))
}
```

# II. Cross-Dataset Parcel Matching Analysis

## II.1. Initial Matching Assessment (With Spaces)

*First attempt to identify common parcels between soil and yield datasets, preserving original spacing*

```{r}
# Step 1: Standardize inputs to uppercase
soil_parcels <- toupper(unique(soil_data$Parc.Detaillee))
yield_parcels <- toupper(unique(data$Parcelle))

# Step 2: Matching statistics
common_parcels <- intersect(soil_parcels, yield_parcels)
only_soil <- setdiff(soil_parcels, yield_parcels)
only_yield <- setdiff(yield_parcels, soil_parcels)

# Step 3: Display results
cat("🔍 Parcel Matching Summary:\n")
cat("• Total unique parcels in SOIL data  :", length(soil_parcels), "\n")
cat("• Total unique parcels in YIELD data :", length(yield_parcels), "\n")
cat("• ✅ Common parcels                  :", length(common_parcels), 
    paste0(" (", round(length(common_parcels) / length(yield_parcels) * 100, 1), "% of yield parcels)\n"))
cat("• ❌ Parcels only in SOIL data      :", length(only_soil), "\n")
cat("• ❌ Parcels only in YIELD data     :", length(only_yield), "\n")

# Step 4: Display samples of mismatches
cat("\n📂 Sample of parcels only in SOIL data:\n")
if (length(only_soil) > 0) {
  print(head(only_soil, 10))
} else {
  cat("✔️ None. All soil parcels are found in yield data.\n")
}

cat("\n📂 Sample of parcels only in YIELD data:\n")
if (length(only_yield) > 0) {
  print(head(only_yield, 10))
} else {
  cat("✔️ None. All yield parcels are found in soil data.\n")
}

```

```{r}
# 1. Define a cleaning function
clean_parcel_name <- function(x) {
  x <- toupper(x)             # Uppercase
  x <- gsub("\\s+", "", x)    # Remove all spaces
  x
}

# 2. Apply cleaning
soil_parcels <- clean_parcel_name(soil_data$Parc.Detaillee)
yield_parcels <- clean_parcel_name(data$Parcelle)

# 3. Unique values after cleaning
soil_parcels_unique <- sort(unique(soil_parcels))
yield_parcels_unique <- sort(unique(yield_parcels))

# 4. Compare
common_parcels <- intersect(soil_parcels_unique, yield_parcels_unique)
only_soil <- setdiff(soil_parcels_unique, yield_parcels_unique)
only_yield <- setdiff(yield_parcels_unique, soil_parcels_unique)

# 5. Display results
cat("🔍 Parcel Matching Summary (After Cleaning):\n")
cat("• Total unique parcels in SOIL data  :", length(soil_parcels_unique), "\n")
cat("• Total unique parcels in YIELD data :", length(yield_parcels_unique), "\n")
cat("• ✅ Common parcels                  :", length(common_parcels),
    paste0(" (", round(length(common_parcels) / length(yield_parcels_unique) * 100, 1), "% of yield parcels)\n"))
cat("• ❌ Parcels only in SOIL data      :", length(only_soil), "\n")
cat("• ❌ Parcels only in YIELD data     :", length(only_yield), "\n")

# 6. Sample of mismatches
cat("\n📂 Sample of parcels only in SOIL data:\n")
if (length(only_soil) > 0) {
  print(head(only_soil, 10))
} else {
  cat("✔️ None. All soil parcels are found in yield data.\n")
}

cat("\n📂 Sample of parcels only in YIELD data:\n")
if (length(only_yield) > 0) {
  print(head(only_yield, 10))
} else {
  cat("✔️ None. All yield parcels are found in soil data.\n")
}

```

### II.1.1. Campaign year parsing and normalization

*Convert "Camp" field (e.g., "03-04") to numeric year (2003) and create standardized parcel names*

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)



cat("Yield data dimensions:", dim(data), "\n")
cat("Yield data columns:\n")
print(colnames(data))

# Extract start year from Camp, e.g. "03-04" -> 2003
data <- data %>%
  mutate(year_start = 2000 + as.numeric(substr(Camp, 1, 2)))

# Normalize parcel names: uppercase + remove spaces
data <- data %>%
  mutate(Parcelle_norm = str_replace_all(str_to_upper(Parcelle), "\\s+", ""))


cat("\nSoil data dimensions:", dim(soil_data), "\n")
cat("Soil data columns:\n")
print(colnames(soil_data))

# Normalize parcel names in soil data + ensure Annee is numeric
soil_data <- soil_data %>%
  mutate(
    Parc.Detaillee_norm = str_replace_all(str_to_upper(Parc.Detaillee), "\\s+", ""),
    Annee = as.numeric(Annee)
  )

# --- Create unique parcel-year keys ---

yield_keys <- data %>%
  distinct(Parcelle_norm, year_start) %>%
  rename(Year = year_start, Parcel = Parcelle_norm)

soil_keys <- soil_data %>%
  distinct(Parc.Detaillee_norm, Annee) %>%
  rename(Year = Annee, Parcel = Parc.Detaillee_norm)

# --- Find common and unique keys ---
common_keys <- inner_join(yield_keys, soil_keys, by = c("Parcel", "Year"))
only_in_yield <- anti_join(yield_keys, soil_keys, by = c("Parcel", "Year"))
only_in_soil <- anti_join(soil_keys, yield_keys, by = c("Parcel", "Year"))

# --- Summary output ---
cat("\n=== Parcel-Year Linkage Summary ===\n")
cat("Total unique parcel-year in yield data: ", nrow(yield_keys), "\n")
cat("Total unique parcel-year in soil data : ", nrow(soil_keys), "\n")
cat("Common parcel-year pairs               : ", nrow(common_keys), "\n")
cat("Parcel-years only in yield data        : ", nrow(only_in_yield), "\n")
cat("Parcel-years only in soil data         : ", nrow(only_in_soil), "\n")

# --- Show samples ---
cat("\nSample parcel-years only in yield data:\n")
print(head(only_in_yield, 10))

cat("\nSample parcel-years only in soil data:\n")
print(head(only_in_soil, 10))


```

## II.2. Enhanced Matching with Name Cleaning (Trimmed)

*Improved matching strategy by removing whitespace inconsistencies that prevent accurate parcel identification*

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)

cat("Yield data dimensions:", dim(data), "\n")
cat("Yield data columns:\n")
print(colnames(data))

# Extract start year from Camp, e.g. "03-04" -> 2003
data <- data %>%
  mutate(year_start = 2000 + as.numeric(substr(Camp, 1, 2)))

# Normalize parcel names: uppercase only, keep spaces
data <- data %>%
  mutate(Parcelle_norm = str_to_upper(Parcelle))

cat("\nSoil data dimensions:", dim(soil_data), "\n")
cat("Soil data columns:\n")
print(colnames(soil_data))

# Normalize parcel names in soil data: uppercase only, keep spaces + ensure Annee is numeric
soil_data <- soil_data %>%
  mutate(
    Parc.Detaillee_norm = str_to_upper(Parc.Detaillee),
    Annee = as.numeric(Annee)
  )

# --- Create unique parcel-year keys ---

yield_keys <- data %>%
  distinct(Parcelle_norm, year_start) %>%
  rename(Year = year_start, Parcel = Parcelle_norm)

soil_keys <- soil_data %>%
  distinct(Parc.Detaillee_norm, Annee) %>%
  rename(Year = Annee, Parcel = Parc.Detaillee_norm)

# --- Find common and unique keys ---
common_keys <- inner_join(yield_keys, soil_keys, by = c("Parcel", "Year"))
only_in_yield <- anti_join(yield_keys, soil_keys, by = c("Parcel", "Year"))
only_in_soil <- anti_join(soil_keys, yield_keys, by = c("Parcel", "Year"))

# --- Summary output ---
cat("\n=== Parcel-Year Linkage Summary (Uppercase only) ===\n")
cat("Total unique parcel-year in yield data: ", nrow(yield_keys), "\n")
cat("Total unique parcel-year in soil data : ", nrow(soil_keys), "\n")
cat("Common parcel-year pairs               : ", nrow(common_keys), "\n")
cat("Parcel-years only in yield data        : ", nrow(only_in_yield), "\n")
cat("Parcel-years only in soil data         : ", nrow(only_in_soil), "\n")

# --- Show samples ---
cat("\nSample parcel-years only in yield data:\n")
print(head(only_in_yield, 10))

cat("\nSample parcel-years only in soil data:\n")
print(head(only_in_soil, 10))



```

### II.1.2. Soil Data Duplicate Analysis

*Identify parcel-year combinations that appear multiple times in the soil dataset*

```{r}
library(dplyr)

soil_duplicates <- soil_data %>%
  mutate(
    Parc.Detaillee_norm = toupper(Parc.Detaillee)
  ) %>%
  group_by(Parc.Detaillee_norm, Annee) %>%
  filter(n() > 1) %>%
  arrange(Parc.Detaillee_norm, Annee)

cat("Number of duplicated parcel-year pairs:", length(unique(paste(soil_duplicates$Parc.Detaillee_norm, soil_duplicates$Annee))), "\n")

# Show a sample of duplicated parcel-year groups
print(head(soil_duplicates, 20))
```

```{r}
# Prepare data for plotting
linkage_counts <- tibble(
  Category = c("Yield Only", "Soil Only", "Common"),
  Count = c(nrow(only_in_yield), nrow(only_in_soil), nrow(common_keys))
)

# ---- 1. Bar plot: Parcel-Year linkage summary ----

plot_linkage <- ggplot(linkage_counts, aes(x = Category, y = Count, fill = Category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::comma(Count)), vjust = -0.5, size = 5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yield Only" = "#1f78b4", "Soil Only" = "#33a02c", "Common" = "#6a3d9a")) +
  labs(title = "Parcel-Year Linkage Summary",
       subtitle = paste0("Yield unique: ", scales::comma(nrow(yield_keys)),
                         " | Soil unique: ", scales::comma(nrow(soil_keys))),
       x = NULL,
       y = "Number of Unique Parcel-Year Pairs") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold"))

# ---- 2. Year distribution plots ----

# Parcel counts by year in yield
yield_year_dist <- yield_keys %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(Parcel_Count = n()) %>%
  ungroup()

plot_yield_year <- ggplot(yield_year_dist, aes(x = Year, y = Parcel_Count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#1f78b4") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty(yield_year_dist$Year, 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Yield Data: Parcel-Year Counts by Year",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Number of Unique Parcels") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

# Parcel counts by year in soil
soil_year_dist <- soil_keys %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(Parcel_Count = n()) %>%
  ungroup()

plot_soil_year <- ggplot(soil_year_dist, aes(x = Year, y = Parcel_Count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#33a02c") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = pretty(soil_year_dist$Year, 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
  labs(title = "Soil Data: Parcel-Year Counts by Year",
       x = "Year",
       y = "Number of Unique Parcels") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13)

# ---- 3. Combined year distributions ----

plot_year_combined <- plot_yield_year | plot_soil_year + 
  plot_annotation(title = "Yearly Distribution of Unique Parcel-Year Combinations",
                  theme = theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold")))

# ---- 4. Pie chart of linkage proportions ----

plot_pie <- ggplot(linkage_counts, aes(x = "", y = Count, fill = Category)) +
  geom_col(width = 1, color = "white") +
  coord_polar("y") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yield Only" = "#1f78b4", "Soil Only" = "#33a02c", "Common" = "#6a3d9a")) +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(Category, "\n", scales::percent(Count / sum(Count), accuracy = 0.1))),
            position = position_stack(vjust = 0.5), size = 5) +
  labs(title = "Proportion of Parcel-Year Linkage Categories") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold"))

# ---- 5. Arrange all plots in a clean layout ----

final_plot <- plot_linkage | plot_pie
combined_plot <- final_plot / plot_year_combined + 
  plot_layout(heights = c(1, 2)) +
  plot_annotation(caption = "Data processed with uppercase parcel names only, spaces preserved.",
                  theme = theme(plot.caption = element_text(size = 11, face = "italic")))

# ---- Print final plot ----
print(combined_plot)
```

# III. Dataset Preparation & Column Renaming

## III.1. English Column Name Translation

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)
library(scales)
library(viridis)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(gridExtra)
library(ggpubr)
library(corrplot)
library(reshape2)

# Set publication-ready theme
publication_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 20)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40", margin = margin(b = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray50", hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray95", size = 0.3),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = NA)
  )

# Color palettes for consistency
color_primary <- "#2E86AB"
color_secondary <- "#A23B72"
color_accent <- "#F18F01"
color_success <- "#4CAF50"
color_warning <- "#FF9800"
color_danger <- "#F44336"

# Create output directory for plots
if (!dir.exists("publication_plots")) {
  dir.create("publication_plots")
}

# Assuming your soil_data is already loaded with the renamed columns
# Each row represents a sampling event for a parcel

# ============================================================================
# PART 1: DATA PREPARATION AND STANDARDIZATION
# ============================================================================

# IMPORTANT: Standardize Plot names to UPPERCASE for consistency
soil_data$Plot <- toupper(as.character(soil_data$Plot))
soil_data$Plot_ID <- toupper(as.character(soil_data$Plot_ID))
soil_data$Detailed_Plot <- toupper(as.character(soil_data$Detailed_Plot))

# Convert Sampling_Date to proper date format if it's not already
soil_data$Sampling_Date <- as.Date(soil_data$Sampling_Date)

# Data quality check after standardization
cat("=== DATA STANDARDIZATION COMPLETE ===\n")
cat("Plot names converted to uppercase\n")
cat("Unique plots after standardization:", length(unique(soil_data$Plot)), "\n")
cat("Sample plot names:", paste(head(unique(soil_data$Plot), 10), collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

# Enhanced sampling summary with additional metrics
sampling_summary <- soil_data %>%
  group_by(Plot) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Samplings = n(),
    First_Sampling_Date = min(Sampling_Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    Last_Sampling_Date = max(Sampling_Date, na.rm = TRUE),
    First_Sampling_Year = min(Year, na.rm = TRUE),
    Last_Sampling_Year = max(Year, na.rm = TRUE),
    Years_Since_Last_Sampling = 2024 - max(Year, na.rm = TRUE),
    Sampling_Period_Years = max(Year, na.rm = TRUE) - min(Year, na.rm = TRUE),
    Average_Years_Between_Samplings = ifelse(n() > 1, 
                                           (max(Year, na.rm = TRUE) - min(Year, na.rm = TRUE)) / (n() - 1), 
                                           NA),
    Sampling_Frequency_Score = case_when(
      n() >= 10 ~ "Very High",
      n() >= 7 ~ "High",
      n() >= 4 ~ "Medium",
      n() >= 2 ~ "Low",
      TRUE ~ "Very Low"
    ),
    Recency_Category = case_when(
      2024 - max(Year, na.rm = TRUE) <= 2 ~ "Recent (≤2 years)",
      2024 - max(Year, na.rm = TRUE) <= 5 ~ "Moderate (3-5 years)",
      2024 - max(Year, na.rm = TRUE) <= 10 ~ "Old (6-10 years)",
      TRUE ~ "Very Old (>10 years)"
    ),
    Sampling_Years = paste(sort(unique(Year)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Samplings))

# Get latest analysis information
latest_records <- soil_data %>%
  group_by(Plot) %>%
  filter(Year == max(Year, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  slice_max(Sampling_Date, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
  select(Plot, Year_Last_Analysis, Year_Before_Last_Analysis, 
         Campaign, Strip, Sample_Type, Depth_cm) %>%
  ungroup()

# Final comprehensive dataset
sampling_analysis <- sampling_summary %>%
  left_join(latest_records, by = "Plot")

# Temporal analysis
yearly_activity <- soil_data %>%
  group_by(Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Samples_Count = n(),
    Unique_Plots = n_distinct(Plot),
    Sampling_Density = n() / n_distinct(Plot),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Year)

# Monthly patterns
monthly_activity <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Sampling_Date)) %>%
  mutate(
    Month = month(Sampling_Date),
    Month_Name = month(Sampling_Date, label = TRUE, abbr = FALSE),
    Season = case_when(
      Month %in% c(6, 7, 8, 9) ~ "Rainy",
      TRUE ~ "Dry"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(Month, Month_Name, Season) %>%
  summarise(
    Samples_Count = n(),
    Unique_Plots = n_distinct(Plot),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )


# Campaign analysis if available
if("Campaign" %in% colnames(soil_data) && sum(!is.na(soil_data$Campaign)) > 0) {
  campaign_analysis <- soil_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(Campaign)) %>%
    group_by(Campaign, Year) %>%
    summarise(
      Samples_Count = n(),
      Unique_Plots = n_distinct(Plot),
      .groups = 'drop'
    )
}

# ============================================================================
# PART 2: PUBLICATION-READY VISUALIZATIONS
# ============================================================================

# PLOT 1: Enhanced Sampling Frequency Distribution
p1 <- ggplot(sampling_analysis, aes(x = Total_Samplings)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, fill = color_primary, alpha = 0.8, color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  geom_text(stat = 'count', aes(label = after_stat(count)), 
            vjust = -0.5, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Soil Sampling Frequency Across Plots",
    subtitle = paste("Analysis of", nrow(sampling_analysis), "plots with", nrow(soil_data), "total sampling events"),
    x = "Number of Sampling Events per Plot",
    y = "Number of Plots",
```

## III.2. Block-level sampling analysis

### III.2.1. Block Extraction from Parcel IDs

*Parse parcel naming conventions to extract block identifiers for hierarchical analysis*

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# BLOCK-LEVEL SAMPLING ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(viridis)
library(gridExtra)
library(ggpubr)
library(knitr)
library(DT)

# Load and prepare data (assuming soil_data is already loaded with renamed columns)
# First, ensure everything is uppercase as requested
soil_data$Detailed_Plot <- toupper(as.character(soil_data$Detailed_Plot))
soil_data$Plot <- toupper(as.character(soil_data$Plot))

# ============================================================================
# STEP 1: EXTRACT BLOCK INFORMATION FROM DETAILED_PLOT
# ============================================================================

extract_block_from_parcel <- function(parcel_id) {
  # Remove any spaces and ensure uppercase
  parcel_id <- gsub("\\s+", "", toupper(parcel_id))
  
  # Extract block using regex patterns
  # Pattern 1: Two letters followed by numbers (e.g., "KH", "MB")
  if (grepl("^[A-Z]{2}[0-9]", parcel_id)) {
    return(substr(parcel_id, 1, 2))
  }
  # Pattern 2: One letter followed by numbers (e.g., "B")
  else if (grepl("^[A-Z][0-9]", parcel_id)) {
    return(substr(parcel_id, 1, 1))
  }
  # Pattern 3: Handle special cases or return first letter as fallback
  else {
    # For any other pattern, take the first sequence of letters
    block_match <- regmatches(parcel_id, regexpr("^[A-Z]+", parcel_id))
    if (length(block_match) > 0) {
      return(block_match[1])
    } else {
      return(NA)
    }
  }
}

# Apply block extraction
soil_data$Block <- sapply(soil_data$Detailed_Plot, extract_block_from_parcel)

# Verify block extraction with examples
cat("=== BLOCK EXTRACTION VERIFICATION ===\n")
block_examples <- soil_data %>%
  select(Detailed_Plot, Block) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(Block, Detailed_Plot) %>%
  head(20)

print(block_examples)
cat("\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 2: COMPREHENSIVE BLOCK ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

# Total number of blocks
unique_blocks <- sort(unique(soil_data$Block[!is.na(soil_data$Block)]))
cat("=== TOTAL BLOCKS IN DATASET ===\n")
cat("Number of unique blocks:", length(unique_blocks), "\n")
cat("Block names:", paste(unique_blocks, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 3: PARCELS PER BLOCK PER YEAR ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

parcels_per_block_year <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Block) & !is.na(Year) & !is.na(Detailed_Plot)) %>%
  group_by(Block, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Unique_Parcels = n_distinct(Detailed_Plot),
    Total_Parcels_List = paste(sort(unique(Detailed_Plot)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Block, Year)

cat("=== UNIQUE PARCELS PER BLOCK PER YEAR ===\n")
print(head(parcels_per_block_year, 20))
cat("\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 4: SAMPLED PARCELS PER BLOCK PER YEAR ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

sampled_parcels_per_block_year <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Block) & !is.na(Year) & !is.na(Detailed_Plot)) %>%
  group_by(Block, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Sampled_Parcels_Count = n_distinct(Detailed_Plot),
    Total_Sampling_Events = n(),
    Average_Samples_Per_Parcel = round(n() / n_distinct(Detailed_Plot), 2),
    Sampled_Parcels_List = paste(sort(unique(Detailed_Plot)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Block, Year)

cat("=== SAMPLED PARCELS PER BLOCK PER YEAR ===\n")
print(head(sampled_parcels_per_block_year, 20))
cat("\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 5: MULTIPLE SAMPLING ANALYSIS (PARCELS SAMPLED 2+ TIMES PER YEAR)
# ============================================================================

multiple_sampling_analysis <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Block) & !is.na(Year) & !is.na(Detailed_Plot)) %>%
  group_by(Block, Year, Detailed_Plot) %>%
  summarise(
    Sampling_Count = n(),
    Sampling_Dates = paste(sort(unique(Sampling_Date)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  filter(Sampling_Count >= 2) %>%
  arrange(Block, Year, desc(Sampling_Count))

multiple_sampling_summary <- multiple_sampling_analysis %>%
  group_by(Block, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Parcels_Sampled_Multiple_Times = n(),
    Max_Samples_Per_Parcel = max(Sampling_Count),
    Total_Multiple_Samples = sum(Sampling_Count),
    Multiple_Sampled_Parcels_List = paste(Detailed_Plot, collapse = ", "),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Block, Year)

cat("=== PARCELS SAMPLED MULTIPLE TIMES PER YEAR ===\n")
cat("Summary by Block and Year:\n")
print(head(multiple_sampling_summary, 15))
cat("\n")

cat("Detailed breakdown of multiple samplings:\n")
print(head(multiple_sampling_analysis, 15))
cat("\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 6: TOTAL SAMPLING EVENTS PER BLOCK PER YEAR
# ============================================================================

sampling_events_per_block_year <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Block) & !is.na(Year)) %>%
  group_by(Block, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Sampling_Events = n(),
    Unique_Parcels_Sampled = n_distinct(Detailed_Plot),
    Average_Samples_Per_Parcel = round(n() / n_distinct(Detailed_Plot), 2),
    Max_Samples_Per_Parcel = max(table(Detailed_Plot)),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Block, Year)

cat("=== TOTAL SAMPLING EVENTS PER BLOCK PER YEAR ===\n")

cat("\n")

# ============================================================================

# Overall block summary
block_overall_summary <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Block)) %>%
  group_by(Block) %>%
  summarise(
    Total_Sampling_Events = n(),

    Average_Samples_Per_Parcel = round(n() / n_distinct(Detailed_Plot), 2),

    .groups = 'drop'

cat("=== OVERALL BLOCK SUMMARY ===\n")
print(block_overall_summary)

# Yearly summary across all blocks
yearly_summary_all_blocks <- soil_data %>%

cat("=== YEARLY SUMMARY ACROSS ALL BLOCKS ===\n")
print(yearly_summary_all_blocks)
cat("\n")

# ============================================================================
# STEP 8: ADVANCED ANALYSIS - SAMPLING INTENSITY AND PATTERNS
# ============================================================================

# Sampling intensity matrix (Block x Year)
sampling_intensity_matrix <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Block) & !is.na(Year)) %>%
  group_by(Block, Year) %>%
  summarise(Sampling_Events = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%

cat("=== SAMPLING INTENSITY MATRIX (Block x Year) ===\n")
print(sampling_intensity_matrix)
cat("\n")

# Block activity patterns
block_activity_patterns <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Block) & !is.na(Year)) %>%

cat("=== BLOCK ACTIVITY PATTERNS ===\n")

# Create output directory

# Export all analysis results

write.csv(sampling_intensity_matrix, "block_analysis_results/sampling_intensity_matrix.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ============================================================================
# STEP 10: KEY FINDINGS SUMMARY
# ============================================================================

cat("📊 DATASET OVERVIEW:\n")
cat("   • Total unique blocks:", length(unique_blocks), "\n")
cat("   • Block names:", paste(unique_blocks, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("   • Total sampling records:", nrow(soil_data), "\n")
cat("   • Records with valid block info:", sum(!is.na(soil_data$Block)), "\n\n")

cat("🏆 TOP PERFORMING BLOCKS (by total samples):\n")
top_blocks <- head(block_overall_summary, 5)
for(i in 1:nrow(top_blocks)) {
  cat(sprintf("   %d. Block %s: %d samples across %d parcels (%d years active)\n", 
              i, top_blocks$Block[i], top_blocks$Total_Sampling_Events[i], 
              top_blocks$Total_Unique_Parcels[i], top_blocks$Years_Active[i]))
}
cat("\n")

cat("📈 SAMPLING TRENDS:\n")
peak_year <- yearly_summary_all_blocks$Year[which.max(yearly_summary_all_blocks$Total_Sampling_Events)]
peak_samples <- max(yearly_summary_all_blocks$Total_Sampling_Events)
cat("   • Peak sampling year:", peak_year, "with", peak_samples, "samples\n")
cat("   • Most active blocks per year:", max(yearly_summary_all_blocks$Active_Blocks), "\n")
cat("   • Years with data:", paste(range(yearly_summary_all_blocks$Year), collapse = "-"), "\n\n")

cat("🔄 MULTIPLE SAMPLING PATTERNS:\n")
total_multiple_parcels <- sum(multiple_sampling_summary$Parcels_Sampled_Multiple_Times, na.rm = TRUE)
cat("   • Total parcel-years with multiple samples:", total_multiple_parcels, "\n")
if(nrow(multiple_sampling_analysis) > 0) {
  max_samples <- max(multiple_sampling_analysis$Sampling_Count)
  cat("   • Maximum samples per parcel in one year:", max_samples, "\n")
  
  # Find the parcel with maximum samples
  max_parcel <- multiple_sampling_analysis[which.max(multiple_sampling_analysis$Sampling_Count), ]
  cat("   • Most intensively sampled parcel:", max_parcel$Detailed_Plot, 
      "in", max_parcel$Year, "(", max_parcel$Sampling_Count, "samples)\n")
}
```

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# VISUALIZATION 9: SAMPLING CONSISTENCY ANALYSIS
# ============================================================================

# Calculate consistency metrics
consistency_data <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Block) & !is.na(Year)) %>%
  group_by(Block, Year) %>%
  summarise(Sampling_Events = n(), .groups = 'drop') %>%
  group_by(Block) %>%
  summarise(
    Mean_Samples = mean(Sampling_Events),
    SD_Samples = sd(Sampling_Events, na.rm = TRUE),
    CV_Samples = ifelse(Mean_Samples > 0, SD_Samples / Mean_Samples, 0),
    Min_Samples = min(Sampling_Events),
    Max_Samples = max(Sampling_Events),
    Consistency_Score = 1 / (1 + CV_Samples), # Higher score = more consistent
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Block = fct_reorder(Block, Consistency_Score),
    Consistency_Category = cut(Consistency_Score,
                             breaks = c(0, 0.5, 0.7, 0.85, 1.0),
                             labels = c("Variable", "Moderate", "Consistent", "Very Consistent"),
                             include.lowest = TRUE)
  )

p9 <- ggplot(consistency_data, aes(x = Block, y = Consistency_Score, fill = Consistency_Category)) +
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8, color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Consistency_Score, 2)), 
            hjust = -0.1, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_brewer(name = "Sampling\nConsistency", type = "seq", palette = "Blues") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Sampling Consistency by Block",
    subtitle = "Consistency score based on coefficient of variation (1 = perfectly consistent)",
    x = "Block",
    y = "Consistency Score",
    caption = "Higher scores indicate more consistent sampling patterns across years"
  ) +
  publication_theme +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.1))

ggsave("block_analysis_plots/09_sampling_consistency.png", p9, 
       width = 12, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = "white")
print(p9)

# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================

# Create a comprehensive summary table for visualization
summary_table_data <- block_overall_summary %>%
  left_join(
    consistency_data %>% select(Block, Consistency_Score, Consistency_Category),
    by = "Block"
  ) %>%
  left_join(
    activity_viz_data %>% select(Block, Activity_Ratio, Efficiency_Category),
    by = "Block"
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Total_Sampling_Events)) %>%
  mutate(
    Rank = row_number(),
    Samples_Per_Parcel = round(Total_Sampling_Events / Total_Unique_Parcels, 2),
    Period = paste(First_Year, Last_Year, sep = "-")
  ) %>%
  select(
    Rank, Block, Total_Sampling_Events, Total_Unique_Parcels, 
    Samples_Per_Parcel, Years_Active, Period, Activity_Ratio, 
    Consistency_Score, Efficiency_Category, Consistency_Category
  )

# Export the summary table
write.csv(summary_table_data, "block_analysis_results/comprehensive_block_summary_table.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ============================================================================
# FINAL SUMMARY AND EXPORT CONFIRMATION
# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================
# ADDITIONAL INSIGHTS GENERATION
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== ADDITIONAL INSIGHTS FROM BLOCK ANALYSIS ===\n")

# Most productive blocks
top_3_blocks <- head(block_overall_summary$Block, 3)
cat("🏆 Top 3 most sampled blocks:", paste(top_3_blocks, collapse = ", "), "\n")

# Blocks needing attention
if(nrow(block_overall_summary) > 0) {
  recent_activity <- soil_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(Block) & Year >= (max(Year, na.rm = TRUE) - 2)) %>%
    distinct(Block) %>%
    pull(Block)
  
  inactive_blocks <- setdiff(unique_blocks, recent_activity)
  if(length(inactive_blocks) > 0) {
    cat("⚠️  Blocks with no recent activity (last 2 years):", paste(inactive_blocks, collapse = ", "), "\n")
  } else {
    cat("✅ All blocks have had recent sampling activity\n")
  }
}

# Sampling efficiency insights
if(exists("consistency_data")) {
  most_consistent <- consistency_data$Block[which.max(consistency_data$Consistency_Score)]
  least_consistent <- consistency_data$Block[which.min(consistency_data$Consistency_Score)]
  cat("📈 Most consistent block:", most_consistent, "\n")
  cat("📉 Most variable block:", least_consistent, "\n")
}
```

### III.2.2. Sampling coverage ratio

```{r}
# ============================================================================
# SAMPLING COVERAGE RATIO HEATMAP
# Ratio of Sampled Plots to Total Available Plots per Block (2003-onwards)
# ============================================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(viridis)
library(scales)

# Set publication theme (matching your existing style)
publication_theme <- theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 16, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5, margin = margin(b = 20)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, color = "gray40", margin = margin(b = 15)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray50", hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 15)),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10),
    legend.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_line(color = "gray95", size = 0.3),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray95", color = NA)
  )

# ============================================================================
# DATA PREPARATION
# ============================================================================

# Step 1: Prepare soil sampling data (number of sampled plots per block-year)
# Filter soil data from 2003 onwards and extract year from campaigns
soil_sampling_data <- soil_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(Block) & !is.na(Year) & Year >= 2003) %>%
  group_by(Block, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    sampled_plots = n_distinct(Detailed_Plot, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  rename(Bloc = Block, Campaign_Year = Year)

# Step 2: Prepare parcel data (total available plots per block-year)
# Convert campaign codes to years and filter from 2003 onwards
parcel_data_processed <- block_parcel_structure %>%
  mutate(
    Campaign_Year = as.numeric(paste0("20", str_sub(Camp, 1, 2)))
  ) %>%
  filter(Campaign_Year >= 2003) %>%
  select(Bloc, Campaign_Year, total_plots = n_parcels)

# Step 3: Merge the datasets to calculate coverage ratio
coverage_ratio_data <- parcel_data_processed %>%
  left_join(soil_sampling_data, by = c("Bloc", "Campaign_Year")) %>%
  mutate(
    sampled_plots = replace_na(sampled_plots, 0),
    coverage_ratio = ifelse(total_plots > 0, sampled_plots / total_plots, 0),
    coverage_percentage = coverage_ratio * 100
  ) %>%
  # Ensure all year-block combinations are present
  complete(Bloc, Campaign_Year = min(Campaign_Year):max(Campaign_Year), 
           fill = list(sampled_plots = 0, total_plots = 0, coverage_ratio = 0, coverage_percentage = 0))

# ============================================================================
# CREATE ENHANCED HEATMAP
# ============================================================================

sampling_coverage_heatmap <- coverage_ratio_data %>%
  mutate(
    Bloc_ordered = factor(Bloc, levels = rev(sort(unique(coverage_ratio_data$Bloc))))
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = factor(Campaign_Year), y = Bloc_ordered, fill = coverage_percentage)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white", size = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(coverage_percentage > 0, 
                               paste0(round(coverage_percentage, 1), "%"), "")), 
            color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name = "Sampling\nCoverage (%)", 
    option = "plasma",
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, "%"),
    limits = c(0, 100),
    na.value = "gray90"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Sampling Coverage Efficiency Heatmap by Block and Year",
    subtitle = "Percentage of available plots sampled per block per year (2003-onwards)",
    x = "Campaign Year",
    y = "Block ID",
    caption = "Percentages show sampling coverage ratio; 100% means all available plots were sampled"
  ) +
  publication_theme +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "right"
  ) +
  guides(fill = guide_colorbar(barwidth = 1, barheight = 8))

# Display the heatmap
print(sampling_coverage_heatmap)

# ============================================================================
# SAVE THE VISUALIZATION
# ============================================================================

# Create output directory if it doesn't exist
if (!dir.exists("sampling_analysis_output")) {
  dir.create("sampling_analysis_output")
}

# Save the heatmap
ggsave("sampling_analysis_output/sampling_coverage_ratio_heatmap.png", 
       sampling_coverage_heatmap, 
       width = 16, height = 10, dpi = 300, bg = "white")

cat("Sampling Coverage Ratio Heatmap saved as 'sampling_coverage_ratio_heatmap.png'\n")

# ============================================================================
# SUMMARY STATISTICS
# ============================================================================

# Calculate summary statistics
summary_stats <- coverage_ratio_data %>%
  filter(total_plots > 0) %>%
  summarise(
    total_block_year_combinations = n(),
    mean_coverage = round(mean(coverage_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    median_coverage = round(median(coverage_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_coverage = round(max(coverage_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    min_coverage = round(min(coverage_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    full_coverage_instances = sum(coverage_percentage >= 100, na.rm = TRUE),
    no_sampling_instances = sum(coverage_percentage == 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Block-level summary
block_summary <- coverage_ratio_data %>%
  filter(total_plots > 0) %>%
  group_by(Bloc) %>%
  summarise(
    years_active = sum(coverage_percentage > 0),
    total_years = n(),
    mean_coverage = round(mean(coverage_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    max_coverage = round(max(coverage_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    activity_ratio = round(years_active / total_years * 100, 1),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_coverage))

# Year-level summary
year_summary <- coverage_ratio_data %>%
  filter(total_plots > 0) %>%
  group_by(Campaign_Year) %>%
  summarise(
    active_blocks = sum(coverage_percentage > 0),
    total_blocks = n(),
    mean_coverage = round(mean(coverage_percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    total_plots_available = sum(total_plots, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_plots_sampled = sum(sampled_plots, na.rm = TRUE),
    overall_coverage = round(total_plots_sampled / total_plots_available * 100, 2),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) %>%
  arrange(Campaign_Year)

# ============================================================================
# EXPORT SUMMARY DATA
# ============================================================================

# Export summary tables
write.csv(coverage_ratio_data, "sampling_analysis_output/coverage_ratio_detailed_data.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(block_summary, "sampling_analysis_output/block_coverage_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(year_summary, "sampling_analysis_output/year_coverage_summary.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# ============================================================================
# PRINT INSIGHTS
# ============================================================================

cat("\n=== SAMPLING COVERAGE ANALYSIS INSIGHTS ===\n")
cat("📊 Overall Statistics (2003-onwards):\n")
cat("   • Mean Coverage Across All Block-Years:", summary_stats$mean_coverage, "%\n")
cat("   • Median Coverage:", summary_stats$median_coverage, "%\n")
cat("   • Maximum Coverage Achieved:", summary_stats$max_coverage, "%\n")
cat("   • Instances of 100%+ Coverage:", summary_stats$full_coverage_instances, "\n")
cat("   • Instances of No Sampling:", summary_stats$no_sampling_instances, "\n\n")

cat("🏆 Top 3 Performing Blocks (by mean coverage):\n")
for(i in 1:min(3, nrow(block_summary))) {
  cat("   ", i, ". Block", block_summary$Bloc[i], 
      "- Mean:", block_summary$mean_coverage[i], 
      "%, Max:", block_summary$max_coverage[i], "%\n")
}

cat("\n📈 Most Active Year:\n")
best_year <- year_summary[which.max(year_summary$overall_coverage), ]
cat("   • Year:", best_year$Campaign_Year, 
    "with", best_year$overall_coverage, "% overall coverage\n")
cat("   • Active Blocks:", best_year$active_blocks, "out of", best_year$total_blocks, "\n")
```

```{r}
# Function to detect outliers using IQR method
detect_outliers <- function(x) {
  q1 <- quantile(x, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
  q3 <- quantile(x, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
  upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
  return(x < lower_bound | x > upper_bound)
}

# Function to add line breaks to long labels
# Corrected function to add line breaks to long labels
format_labels <- function(labels, max_length = 12) {
  sapply(labels, function(x) {
    # Convert to character and handle NA values
    x <- as.character(x)
    if (is.na(x) || x == "NA") {
      return(x)
    }
    
    if (nchar(x) > max_length) {
      # Find good break points (spaces, underscores, or parentheses)
      words <- strsplit(x, "[ _()]")[[1]]
      # Remove empty strings that might result from splitting
      words <- words[words != ""]
      
      if (length(words) > 1) {
        mid_point <- ceiling(length(words) / 2)
        # Safely handle the word splitting
        first_part <- words[1:min(mid_point, length(words))]
        second_part <- words[max(1, mid_point + 1):length(words)]
        
        # Remove any NA values that might have been created
        first_part <- first_part[!is.na(first_part)]
        second_part <- second_part[!is.na(second_part)]
        
        # Only create line break if both parts exist
        if (length(first_part) > 0 && length(second_part) > 0) {
          paste(paste(first_part, collapse = " "), 
                paste(second_part, collapse = " "), sep = "\n")
        } else {
          x  # Return original if splitting didn't work
        }
      } else {
        # If no good break points found, try to break at mid-point
        if (nchar(x) > max_length * 1.5) {
          mid_char <- ceiling(nchar(x) / 2)
          paste(substr(x, 1, mid_char), substr(x, mid_char + 1, nchar(x)), sep = "\n")
        } else {
          x  # Return original if not too long
        }
      }
    } else {
      x  # Return original if short enough
    }
  }, USE.NAMES = FALSE)  # Add USE.NAMES = FALSE to avoid naming issues
}

# Enhanced function to create narrow boxplots with red outlier detection
create_enhanced_boxplot <- function(data_long, title, subtitle, colors, x_label, y_label, 
                                  variable_col = "variable", value_col = "value", remove_outliers = FALSE) {
  
  # Detect outliers for each variable
  data_with_outliers <- data_long %>%
    group_by(!!sym(variable_col)) %>%
    mutate(
      is_outlier = detect_outliers(!!sym(value_col)),
      outlier_label = ifelse(is_outlier, "Outlier", "Normal")
    ) %>%
    ungroup()
  
  # Remove outliers if requested
  if (remove_outliers) {
    plot_data <- data_with_outliers %>% filter(!is_outlier)
    title <- paste(title, "(Without Outliers)")
  } else {
    plot_data <- data_with_outliers
  }
  
  # Format labels for better display
  plot_data[[variable_col]] <- format_labels(plot_data[[variable_col]])
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes_string(x = variable_col, y = value_col, fill = variable_col)) +
    geom_boxplot(
      alpha = 0.85, 
      outlier.shape = NA,
      width = 0.18,
      color = "#000000",
      size = 0.6,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    # Add red outlier points manually
    {if (!remove_outliers) {
      geom_point(
        data = plot_data %>% filter(is_outlier),
        aes_string(x = variable_col, y = value_col),
        color = "#DC143C",
        size = 1.2,
        alpha = 0.8,
        shape = 16,
        inherit.aes = FALSE
      )
    }} +
    stat_summary(
      fun = median, 
      geom = "text", 
      aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", after_stat(y))),
      size = 2.2,
      color = "white", 
      fontface = "bold",
      vjust = 0.5
    ) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = colors) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = subtitle,
      x = x_label,
      y = y_label
    ) +
    publication_theme +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.01)) +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off")
  
  return(p)
}

# 9. COMPREHENSIVE CORRELATION MATRIX - CORRECTED VERSION
# ============================================================================
cat("Creating comprehensive correlation matrix...\n")

# Select key numeric variables for correlation analysis with proper data cleaning
key_variables <- soil_data %>%
  select(pH, Electrical_Conductivity_mmho_cm, Exchangeable_Calcium_meq_100g,
         Exchangeable_Magnesium_meq_100g, Exchangeable_Sodium_meq_100g, 
         Exchangeable_Potassium_meq_100g, Available_P2O5_mg_kg,
         Clay_percent, Fine_Silt_percent, Coarse_Silt_percent,
         Fine_Sand_percent, Coarse_Sand_percent, Organic_Carbon_per_mille,
         Total_Nitrogen_per_mille, CEC_meq_100g, PF_4.2, PF_2.5,
         Organic_Matter_percent, CN_Ratio, Sum_of_Exchangeable_Bases_meq_100g,
         CaO_g_100g, Calculated_T_Saturation, Mg_Ca_Ratio, Mg_K_Ratio) %>%
  # Convert all columns to numeric, handling any conversion issues
  mutate_all(~as.numeric(as.character(.))) %>%
  # Keep only variables with at least 10 non-NA values
  select_if(~sum(!is.na(.)) > 10) %>%
  # Remove rows with too many NAs (keep rows with at least 5 non-NA values)
  filter(rowSums(!is.na(.)) >= 5)

# Only proceed if we have enough data
if(ncol(key_variables) >= 3 && nrow(key_variables) >= 10) {
  
  # Method 1: Using Hmisc::rcorr (preferred method with significance testing)
  tryCatch({
    cor_result <- rcorr(as.matrix(key_variables), type = "pearson")
    cor_matrix <- cor_result$r
    p_matrix <- cor_result$P
    
    # Clean correlation matrix
    cor_matrix[is.na(cor_matrix)] <- 0
    cor_matrix[is.infinite(cor_matrix)] <- 0
    diag(cor_matrix) <- 1
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Hmisc method failed, using base R correlation...\n")
    
    # Method 2: Fallback using base R correlation
    cor_matrix <- cor(key_variables, use = "pairwise.complete.obs", method = "pearson")
    cor_matrix[is.na(cor_matrix)] <- 0
    cor_matrix[is.infinite(cor_matrix)] <- 0
    diag(cor_matrix) <- 1
    p_matrix <- NULL
  })
  
  # Create enhanced correlation plot
  png("Soil_Analysis_Publication/09_Comprehensive_Correlation_Matrix.png", 
      width = 10, height = 8, units = "in", res = 300, bg = "white")
  
  par(mar = c(2, 2, 4, 2))
  
  corr_colors <- colorRampPalette(c("#053061", "#2166AC", "#4393C3", "#92C5DE", 
                                   "#D1E5F0", "#F7F7F7", 
                                   "#FDDBC7", "#F4A582", "#D6604D", "#B2182B", "#67001F"))(100)
  
  corrplot(cor_matrix,
           method = "color",
           type = "upper",
           order = "hclust",
           col = corr_colors,
           tl.col = "#000000",
           tl.srt = 45,
           tl.cex = 0.8,
           tl.font = 2,
           cl.cex = 1.0,
           title = "Correlation Matrix of Key Soil Variables\n(Pearson Correlation Coefficients)",
           mar = c(0,0,3,0),
           diag = FALSE,
           addCoef.col = "#000000",
           number.cex = 0.5,
           number.digits = 2,
           number.font = 1,
           outline = TRUE,
           cl.ratio = 0.15)
  
  # Add significance stars if p_matrix is available
  if(!is.null(p_matrix)) {
    n_vars <- ncol(cor_matrix)
    for(i in 1:(n_vars-1)) {
      for(j in (i+1):n_vars) {
        if(!is.na(p_matrix[i,j])) {
          if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.001) {
            sig_symbol <- "***"
          } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.01) {
            sig_symbol <- "**"
          } else if(p_matrix[i,j] < 0.05) {
            sig_symbol <- "*"
          } else {
            sig_symbol <- ""
          }
          
          if(sig_symbol != "" && !is.na(cor_matrix[i,j]) && abs(cor_matrix[i,j]) > 0.1) {
            x_center <- j
            y_center <- n_vars - i + 1
            text(x_center, y_center + 0.25, sig_symbol, 
                 cex = 0.6, col = "#000000", font = 2)
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  dev.off()
  
} else {
  cat("Insufficient data for correlation analysis\n")
}

# Enhanced function to create histogram with normal overlay - CORRECTED VERSION
create_histogram <- function(data, variable, title, color, x_label) {
  
  # Clean the data first
  data_clean_values <- as.numeric(as.character(data[[variable]]))
  data_clean_values <- data_clean_values[!is.na(data_clean_values)]
  
  # Return NULL if insufficient data
  if(length(data_clean_values) < 10) {
    cat("Insufficient data for", variable, "histogram\n")
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Create a clean data frame for plotting
  plot_data <- data.frame(
    values = data_clean_values
  )
  
  # Calculate statistics for normal overlay
  mean_val <- mean(data_clean_values)
  sd_val <- sd(data_clean_values)
  min_val <- min(data_clean_values)
  max_val <- max(data_clean_values)
  
  # Calculate bin width
  n_bins <- min(30, max(10, length(data_clean_values) / 10))
  bin_width <- (max_val - min_val) / n_bins
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = values)) +
    geom_histogram(bins = n_bins, fill = color, color = "#000000", alpha = 0.7, boundary = 0) +
    geom_density(aes(y = after_stat(density) * length(data_clean_values) * bin_width),
                color = "#DC143C", size = 1.2) +
    stat_function(fun = function(x) dnorm(x, mean = mean_val, sd = sd_val) * 
                  length(data_clean_values) * bin_width,
                  color = "#2F4F4F", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = "Red: actual density, Dashed: normal distribution",
      x = x_label,
      y = "Frequency"
    ) +
    publication_theme +
    theme(
      plot.margin = margin(15, 15, 15, 15),  # Increased margins to prevent overlap
      axis.title.x = element_text(margin = margin(t = 12)),  # More space above x-axis title
      axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 12)),  # More space to right of y-axis title
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5),   # Horizontal x-axis labels
      plot.title = element_text(margin = margin(b = 8)),     # Space below title
      plot.subtitle = element_text(margin = margin(b = 12))  # Space below subtitle
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 0.01)) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::number_format(accuracy = 1))
  
  return(p)
}

# 14. OUTLIER ANALYSIS REPORT
# ============================================================================
cat("Generating outlier analysis report...\n")

# Function to calculate outlier statistics
calculate_outlier_stats <- function(data, variable_name) {
  x <- data[[variable_name]]
  x_clean <- x[!is.na(x)]
  
  if(length(x_clean) < 10) return(NULL)
  
  q1 <- quantile(x_clean, 0.25)
  q3 <- quantile(x_clean, 0.75)
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  lower_bound <- q1 - 1.5 * iqr
  upper_bound <- q3 + 1.5 * iqr
  
  outliers <- x_clean[x_clean < lower_bound | x_clean > upper_bound]
  
  data.frame(
    Variable = variable_name,
    Total_Observations = length(x_clean),
    Number_of_Outliers = length(outliers),
    Outlier_Percentage = round((length(outliers) / length(x_clean)) * 100, 2),
    Q1 = round(q1, 3),
    Q3 = round(q3, 3),
    IQR = round(iqr, 3),
    Lower_Bound = round(lower_bound, 3),
    Upper_Bound = round(upper_bound, 3),
    Min_Outlier = ifelse(length(outliers) > 0, round(min(outliers), 3), NA),
    Max_Outlier = ifelse(length(outliers) > 0, round(max(outliers), 3), NA)
  )
}

# Calculate outlier statistics for key variables
key_vars <- c("pH", "Electrical_Conductivity_mmho_cm", "Exchangeable_Calcium_meq_100g",
              "Exchangeable_Magnesium_meq_100g", "Available_P2O5_mg_kg", "Clay_percent",
              "Organic_Matter_percent", "CEC_meq_100g", "Total_Nitrogen_per_mille")

outlier_analysis <- map_dfr(key_vars, ~calculate_outlier_stats(soil_data, .x)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(Variable)) %>%
  arrange(desc(Outlier_Percentage))

# Save outlier analysis
write.csv(outlier_analysis, "Soil_Analysis_Publication/Outlier_Analysis.csv", row.names = FALSE)

print("=== OUTLIER ANALYSIS SUMMARY ===")
print(outlier_analysis)

# ============================================================================
# 15. FINAL SUMMARY AND DATA QUALITY REPORT
# ============================================================================
cat("Generating final data quality report...\n")

# Data completeness analysis
completeness_analysis <- soil_data %>%
  summarise_all(~sum(!is.na(.))) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(), names_to = "Variable", values_to = "Complete_Count") %>%
  mutate(
    Total_Rows = nrow(soil_data),
    Completeness_Percentage = round((Complete_Count / Total_Rows) * 100, 2),
    Missing_Count = Total_Rows - Complete_Count
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(Completeness_Percentage)) %>%
  filter(Complete_Count > 0)  # Remove completely empty columns

# Save completeness analysis
write.csv(completeness_analysis, "Soil_Analysis_Publication/Data_Completeness_Analysis.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# Generate final report
final_report <- list(
  dataset_overview = list(
    total_rows = nrow(soil_data),
    total_columns = ncol(soil_data),
    numeric_columns = sum(sapply(soil_data, is.numeric)),
    character_columns = sum(sapply(soil_data, is.character))
  ),
  key_statistics = list(
    variables_with_data = nrow(completeness_analysis),
    average_completeness = round(mean(completeness_analysis$Completeness_Percentage), 2),
    variables_over_90_complete = sum(completeness_analysis$Completeness_Percentage >= 90),
    variables_over_50_complete = sum(completeness_analysis$Completeness_Percentage >= 50)
  ),
  outlier_summary = list(
    variables_analyzed_for_outliers = nrow(outlier_analysis),
    average_outlier_percentage = round(mean(outlier_analysis$Outlier_Percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
    variables_high_outliers = sum(outlier_analysis$Outlier_Percentage > 10, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
)

# Save final report as JSON
library(jsonlite)
write_json(final_report, "Soil_Analysis_Publication/Final_Analysis_Report.json", pretty = TRUE)



cat("KEY FINDINGS:\n")
cat("• Total observations: ", nrow(soil_data), "\n")
cat("• Variables analyzed: ", nrow(completeness_analysis), "\n")
cat("• Average data completeness: ", round(mean(completeness_analysis$Completeness_Percentage), 1), "%\n")
cat("• Variables with >90% complete data: ", sum(completeness_analysis$Completeness_Percentage >= 90), "\n")

if(nrow(outlier_analysis) > 0) {
  cat("• Average outlier percentage: ", round(mean(outlier_analysis$Outlier_Percentage, na.rm = TRUE), 1), "%\n")
  high_outlier_vars <- outlier_analysis %>% 
    filter(Outlier_Percentage > 10) %>% 
    pull(Variable)
  if(length(high_outlier_vars) > 0) {
    cat("• Variables with high outlier rates (>10%): ", paste(head(high_outlier_vars, 3), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  }
}
```

```{r}
} else if(nrow(cec_pf_variables) > 0) {

  })
  
} else {
  cat("✗ No valid data available for CEC and Water Retention analysis.\n")
  
  # Create a diagnostic summary of the raw data
  cat("\nDiagnostic - Raw data samples:\n")
  cat("CEC_meq_100g samples (first 10):\n")

}
```
